first_step.derivation: Let a state after k rounds be S_k=(R_k,B_k,G_k), with nonnegative integer counts. Initially S_0=(3,2,1), so the total is N_0=3+2+1=6. For any state (r,b,g), put N=r+b+g. A uniform draw gives color probabilities proportional to the current counts: P(red | (r,b,g))=r/N, P(blue | (r,b,g))=b/N, and P(green | (r,b,g))=g/N. The update rules then determine the next state. If red is drawn, the red ball is returned and one blue ball is added, so (r,b,g) goes to (r,b+1,g). If blue is drawn, the blue ball is removed and one green ball is added, so (r,b,g) goes to (r,b-1,g+1). If green is drawn, the green ball is returned and one red ball is added, so (r,b,g) goes to (r+1,b,g). Thus one round has a state-dependent transition kernel. The total changes by +1 on red or green draws and stays the same on a blue draw, because blue is removed and green is added. This step only fixes notation and the transition rules; it does not evaluate any multi-round probability.
